summary.title: Anomalous Hall effect from nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling
summary.authors: Longju Yu, Hong Jian Zhao, Yurong Yang, Laurent Bellaiche, and Yanming Ma
summary.executive_summary: This study establishes a phenomenological theory for the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) driven by nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling, a mechanism largely unexplored compared to linear counterparts. First-principles calculations on Cr2O3 and CoF2 confirm these predictions, showing large anomalous Hall conductivities (up to 200 S/cm) driven by specific electric field configurations. judge_context:
Executive Summary
This study establishes a phenomenological theory for the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) driven by nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling, a mechanism largely unexplored compared to linear counterparts. By analyzing magnetic point groups (MPGs), the authors demonstrate that 90 type-I and type-III MPGs can host AHE induced by uni-axial, bi-axial, or tri-axial electric fields. The theory predicts that these conductivities are reversible upon reversing magnetic order parameters. First-principles calculations on Cr2O3 and CoF2 confirm these predictions, showing large anomalous Hall conductivities (up to 200 S/cm) driven by specific electric field configurations. The work highlights the potential of nonlinear coupling for probing magnetic orders in spintronics, offering new avenues for data readout in memory devices without requiring spontaneous magnetization in all cases.

Research Context
The anomalous Hall effect is a topology-related transport phenomenon. AHE enables efficient probing of magnetic orders in spintronics. Recent studies reveal electric-field induced AHE via linear coupling. AHE from nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling remains largely unexplored. External fields capable of inducing magnetization should induce AHE.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study aims to establish theory for spontaneous and field-driven AHE. Symmetry analysis predicts AHE in a wide variety of magnetic point groups. Nonlinear coupling allows AHE driven by uni-axial, bi-axial, or tri-axial fields. The induced conductivities are reversible by reversing magnetic orders. Cr2O3 and CoF2 are predicted candidates for this nonlinear AHE.

Methodological Details
The study uses a group-theoretical approach for symmetry analysis. Analysis covers 122 magnetic point groups in total. Type-II MPGs are omitted as they forbid magnetization. 90 type-I and type-III MPGs are analyzed for AHE components. First-principles calculations are used to verify theoretical predictions. Cr2O3 has a N´eel temperature of 307 K. CoF2 has a N´eel temperature of 39 K. Materials have no more than 10 ions per primitive cell. The MAGNDATA database was used to select candidate materials.

Procedures And Architectures
AHE is characterized by Jα = P β σαβEβ with transverse conductivity. The Hall vector M behaves like the magnetization vector M. Onsager reciprocity requires σαβ(+L) = σβα(−L). This yields σαβ(+L) = −σαβ(−L) due to anti-symmetric feature. Effective magnetic field Bα_eff is expanded with respect to electric field. Expansion includes linear, second-order, and third-order magnetoelectric couplings. Effective fields for 90 MPGs are derived in Supplementary Note 2. Calculations compute anomalous Hall conductivity components vs chemical potential. Electric field magnitudes used are 4 MV/cm for Cr2O3. Electric field magnitudes used are 4 MV/cm or 2√2 MV/cm for CoF2.

Key Results
90 type-I and type-III MPGs host spontaneous or field-driven AHE. Cr2O3 exhibits σzy, σxz, and σyx driven by Ex, Ey, and Ez. Induced conductivities in Cr2O3 are larger than 100 S/cm. Cr2O3 conductivities are driven by first-order response. Cr2O3 σyx driven by Ey via third-order response is less than 20 S/cm. Reversing magnetic order reverses the sign of AHE in Cr2O3. CoF2 conductivities respond to electric field via second order. CoF2 σyx driven by Ex or Ey yields conductivity larger than 200 S/cm. Reversing magnetic order in CoF2 reverses the anomalous Hall conductivities.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
AHE conductivities are governed by magnetic point group symmetries. Nonlinear coupling creates exotic transport phenomena. The work offers alternative avenues for probing magnetic orders. Opposite magnetic orders yield AHE with opposite signs. This enriches means for detecting magnetic order parameters. This is of practical importance for spintronics applications.

Contradictions And Limitations
Type-II MPGs do not host electric-field induced magnetization. Some MPGs show quenching behavior under specific bi-axial fields. Higher-order responses are omitted in Table I for brevity. Specific mechanisms for identical field components are separated by space. The study focuses on intrinsic mechanisms of AHE.

Claims
Nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling enables electric-field driven AHE in 90 type-I and type-III MPGs. A large variety of magnetic point groups host an AHE. 90 type-I and type-III MPGs are listed in Table I. Type-II MPGs do not host electric-field induced magnetization. Offers alternative avenues for the probe of magnetic orders.
Cr2O3 and CoF2 exhibit large AHE driven by nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling. Cr2O3 and CoF2 are suggested as candidates. CoF2 σyx can reach larger than 200 S/cm. Cr2O3 σyx via third-order response is less than 20 S/cm. Enriches means for detecting magnetic order parameters.

Data And Code Availability
Supplementary Tables 9, 10, 11, and 12 are referenced. MAGNDATA database was used for material selection.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Symmetry analysis covers all 122 MPGs. First-principles calculations verify theoretical predictions. Quenching behavior is noted for specific field directions.

Ethical Considerations
Support acknowledged from National Natural Science Foundation of China. Support acknowledged from Strategic 373 Priority Research Program. L.B. acknowledges Vannevar Bush Faculty Fellowship.

Key Figures Tables
Table I lists 90 type-I and type-III MPGs with AHE components. Fig. 1 shows crystal and magnetic structures for Cr2O3 and CoF2. Figs. 2(a)-(d) depict AHE in Cr2O3. Figs. 2(e)-(h) show AHE in CoF2.

Three Takeaways
1. Nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling enables AHE in 90 type-I and type-III MPGs. 2. Cr2O3 and CoF2 show large AHE driven by nonlinear coupling. 3. The work offers new avenues for probing magnetic orders in spintronics.
